request: a which-house-are-you quiz for my friends with a magic school vibe, so we can all post our results in the chat

design.pitch: Eight snap questions against a burning candle, and Brambleford Academy's Lantern tells you if you're a Moonwarden, Emberjack, Thornquill or Hearthmoss, with a crest to post in the group chat.
design.verb: Read a question, then tap one of four shuffled answers on instinct before the candle burns down; each answer adds 2 to one house and 1 to another.
design.twist: There are no right answers but you can still lose: answering fast scores Conviction, letting the candle burn out twice puts the Lantern out, and a split heart (top two houses less than 2 points apart) can't be sorted. The reveal quotes your own deciding answer back as 'Your tell'.
arc: Questions 1–2: a 1.5 s read lock dims the answers, then the candle bar drains over 9 s; a pick bursts particles in its house's colour and that house's crest along the bottom pops.
Questions 3–8: the four crests glow brighter as you lean toward them; let a candle burn out and 'Your candle gutters…' costs one of your 2 lives.

Reveal: the brass lantern swings over cycling crests ('The Lantern is deciding…') for 1.8 s, then 'THE LANTERN HAS CHOSEN': your crest under rays, 'You are a', the house name, motto, blurb, 'Your tell: “…”' and the share line ('I’m a Moonwarden 🌙').
design.lose: Let the candle run out on two questions and the Lantern goes dark; or finish all 8 with your top two houses less than 2 points apart and 'THE LANTERN FLICKERS': 'Torn between' both house names, with both crests tilted side by side.
design.win: Finish with one house at least 2 points ahead and the Lantern sorts you into it. Conviction counts 10 per answer plus up to 9 more for answering before the candle drains, and 5 points for every point your house leads the runner-up.
juice: Picking an answer: the card bounces, 16 particles in the house's colour burst from it, a light haptic, and that house's crest pops to 1.35x.
The Lantern chooses: a 'shimmer', 48 house-coloured particles plus 24 pale gold sparks, a success haptic, and the crest scales up from 0.2 under slowly turning rays.
A split heart: a 'fall' sound, a 6 px shake and a warning haptic under 'THE LANTERN FLICKERS', then 'Tap to try again'.
design.look: Midnight at a wizard academy: an indigo starry sky with a crescent moon, glowing lanterns at the edges and a castle skyline at the bottom; hushed and candlelit, gold (#F5C66B) on indigo (#150F35). There's no player sprite: you face the candle bar (it turns red below 30%), the answers are cards, and each house has a crest colour (Moonwarden blue, Emberjack orange, Thornquill green, Hearthmoss gold). Baskerville.
design.voice: Whimsical and warm, a cozy boarding-school narrator with dry jokes: 'A toad with strong opinions about your essays', 'Saying yes to every plan, then inventing three more', and the Hearthmoss motto '“Nobody eats alone.”'.

brief.intent: An eight-question personality quiz that sorts you into one of four invented houses of a wizard academy and ends with a shareable crest
brief.audience: friends in a group chat comparing results
brief.competition: none: compare results (with a conviction score on the side)

why_its_good: Weighted answers (+2 to one house, +1 to a second) across four invented houses that are friend-group roles (the 2 a.m. listener, the chaos starter, the loophole finder, the snack bringer), and the reveal quotes your own deciding answer back (`Your tell: “…”`), so the result feels personal and is worth a screenshot.

Stakes without right answers: a candle drains on every question and scores conviction (answer on instinct for more points), hesitating twice puts the Lantern out (`lives` bound to `hesitated`), and a split heart (top two houses within 1 point) ends in a 'Torn between Moonwarden and Emberjack' loss that still names both houses.

Paced for people: a 1.5 s read lock per question, answers that pop and dim, crests along the bottom that glow as you lean toward them, a swinging-lantern drumroll, then a crest reveal with rays, house-coloured particles and a one-line share card ('I’m a Moonwarden 🌙').
pitfalls_avoided: Not `too_short`: the read lock, a 650 ms beat after each answer and the 1.8 s drumroll keep bot runs at 22–28 s (Muse's own quiz ended in 5 s).

Not `cant_lose`: two real lose paths (hesitation, and the Torn ending through an `{"end": "lose"}` effect), so 3 of 5 bots lose; the win is an `{"end": "win"}` effect too, never invented feedback syntax like `{"action": ...}`.
Parameters inside their ranges (`lives.count` 2 of 1..9) and `score`'s `point` really emitted (base 10 per answer, the time bonus added on top), so there's no unreachable fragment rule.
Every tap target is a transparent `rect` over its sprite, so both the hit-test and the playtest bots find the answers.
themes: harry potter sorting hat hogwarts house personality buzzfeed quiz which are you

request: a gossip trivia game at a fancy prep school where you guess who wrote each anonymous post, so I can challenge my roommate to beat my score

design.pitch: Someone keeps posting on Kestrel Hall's anonymous Whisper Wall: guess which of five students (or the dean's corgi) wrote each post, and beat Jules's 1600.
design.verb: Read each anonymous post as it types in, then tap which of the four suspects shown wrote it, within 10 seconds.
design.twist: Every suspect writes in an unmistakable voice (Sloane's 'Per my last', Jasper's secret haikus, Wren's 6:00 sharp, Rafi's stairwell gum, Duchess in ALL CAPS), so each post is a fair deduction, and you're racing a named friend's score, not just running up a total.
arc: 0–10 s: post 1 types onto the glossy card ('anon  ·  the Whisper Wall', 'POST 1 / 12') behind a ▍ cursor for 1.2 s while a blocker covers the answers, then you pick from four suspects.
10–40 s: each new post arrives with a two-note ping; right calls build the Streak (max 3), so a post is worth 100, then 150, then 200, and 'Three in a row! 200 a post now' pops up.

40 s+: the race to pass 'Beat Jules: 1600' before 'POST 12 / 12', which takes at least 9 right calls; a wrong call resets the streak and costs a crown, and six in a row brings 'Six straight. Jules is sweating.'
design.lose: Three wrong calls (running out the 10 s counts as wrong) cost all three crowns; 12 posts without passing 1600 loses; and so does the 180 s time limit.
design.win: You win the moment your score passes Jules's 1600. A right call scores 50 plus 50 × the Streak (max 3): 100, 150, then 200 a post.
juice: A new post: a two-note triangle ping (E6, B6) and the text typing in behind a ▍ cursor.
A right call: a 'sparkle' (plus a 'rise' once the streak is going), and the tilted 'CALLED IT' stamp slams onto the card in mint at 1.7x and settles.
A wrong call: 'IT WAS RAFI' (or whoever it was) stamps on in red, the screen shakes 6 px with a warning haptic, and a gold crown goes.
design.look: Prep-school drama after dark: a plum-velvet backdrop with a faint gold lattice, a pink spotlight, dark arches with ivy and a faint crest; glamorous and sly, mint (#4FE0B0) for right calls and hot pink (#FF5FA2) for gossip. There's no player sprite: the post sits on a glossy card with a pink-to-lilac top bar and a masked avatar, the suspects are pill buttons, and lives are gold crowns. Futura.
design.voice: Sassy, petty and funny, a different voice per suspect: 'Reminder: the library opens at 6:00, not 6:05. Some of us fit three study blocks in before breakfast.', 'Wrote a haiku for my dog, Pancake. He ate it. Honestly? Fair review.', 'THE MAIL CARRIER HAS RETURNED. HE IS A TRAITOR. I HAVE WARNED THIS SCHOOL BEFORE.'

brief.intent: Read anonymous posts from a school confession wall and pick which of five original students (or the dean's corgi) wrote each, racing a friend's score
brief.audience: two friends, one challenging the other

why_its_good: Five original suspects with unmistakable voices (the queen bee's 'per my last', the lacrosse captain's secret haiku, the overachiever's 6:00 sharp, the clown's stairwell gum racket, the corgi's ALL CAPS) make every post a fair deduction, and each question keeps a confuser in the choices (a sailing brag: Sloane or Jasper? a dog haiku: Jasper or the corgi?).

Built for a challenge: `beat_target` shows 'Beat Jules: 1600' and wins the moment you pass it; `combo` streaks make a right answer worth 100 to 200, so one slip can cost the crown; three wrong calls, or 12 posts without passing Jules, lose.
Feels like a feed: each post types in with a cursor and a notification ping, then a stamped verdict ('CALLED IT' or 'IT WAS RAFI') pops on the card while the quiz tints the right and wrong answers.
pitfalls_avoided: The `quiz` fragment's question line doesn't wrap, so the game hands it blank questions (the same number as the posts) and draws its own wrapped post card, instead of overflowing long text.
A transparent blocker over the answers while a post types in gives people time to read and stops instant taps: bot runs take 18–28 s, not 5.

One score system: `score`'s `point` bound to `answered_right` plus one bonus rule (`50 * combo`), with `lives` bound to `answered_wrong` so wrong answers can lose; choices are written exactly as the answers, 4 per question, as `quiz` requires.
themes: gossip girl prep school rich kids drama anonymous who said it trivia

request: a daily space puzzle for our group chat, like decoding a secret message from a rebel ship

design.pitch: Crack three scrambled transmissions from the Driftwood Fleet one letter at a time before the Regency's jammer cuts the line, and the whole group chat gets the same three today.
design.verb: Tap a letter on the keyboard that you think is in the message; a right guess unscrambles every copy of it in the coded grid.
design.twist: It's a real substitution cipher, not hangman: every letter is shown as its neighbour in a shuffled key (none stands for itself), so repeated code letters and word shapes are clues, and each copy a guess reveals scores 10, so common letters pay more.
arc: 0–10 s (Message 1 of 3): 'Tap a letter you think is in the message.' Up to four lines of amber code letters sit under blank cells, and a first guess like E or T lights up copies across the grid.

10–40 s: each guess takes a 450 ms decrypt beat while unknown cells flicker with static; a miss ('No Q. Static on the line.') drops a signal bar, and the navigator's 'Hint (2)' reveals a letter for no points.
40 s+ (Messages 2–3): 'New key. Same crew. Go.' Each message brings a fresh key and three fresh signal bars, while the JAMMER countdown turns red under 15 s.
design.lose: Three wrong letters in one message kill the signal (you get 3 again for each message), or the 120 s jammer arrives before all three are cracked.
design.win: Crack all three messages before the jammer. A right letter scores 10 for each copy in the message, cracking one adds 30 for each signal bar left ('Cracked! +90 for signal left'), and the navigator's tips score nothing.
juice: A right guess: every copy of the letter pops in mint at 1.8x and settles, with a 'chirp', up to 40 mint particles (8 per copy) and a light haptic; three or more copies add an 'arpeggio'.
A miss: a 'zap', a 6 px shake and the status line 'No Q. Static on the line.' as a signal bar goes dark.
Cracking a message: 'Cracked! +90 for signal left' in mint, 60 amber particles burst and fall, and a success haptic, then the next transmission comes in.
design.look: A rebel freighter's comms console in deep space: a navy void with pink and teal nebulae and scattered stars, behind a console with amber brackets; clever and calm. There's no player sprite: decoded letters glow mint (#5CF2C2) above amber (#FFB347) code letters, unknown cells flicker with static, lives are mint signal bars, and the JAMMER timer turns red (#FF5C7A). Avenir Next, with Menlo for the code and the timer.
design.voice: Deadpan spy-radio comedy, each message written with | line breaks: 'the toaster|is a traitor', 'the admiral|is a hologram|act normal', 'hide the map|inside the|space goat'.

brief.intent: A daily cryptogram: three short scrambled transmissions from an original rebel crew, decoded one letter at a time before the jammer arrives
brief.audience: a group chat that plays the same puzzle every day

why_its_good: A real cryptogram, not plain hangman: each message is shown in a substitution cipher (a shuffled key where each letter becomes the next one in that order, so none stands for itself), so word shapes and repeated letters are clues; a right letter unscrambles every copy and scores per copy, so E is worth more than Q.

Three short transmissions per run, each with a new key and fresh signal bars, with deadpan payoffs ('the toaster is a traitor', 'the senate hates our sea shanties'); unknown letters flicker during a short decrypt beat, and a navigator tip (`hint`, twice per run) rescues a stuck player.
Daily and social: `daily_seed` labels it and the host's seed gives the whole Group the same three messages and keys, so scores compare fairly.
pitfalls_avoided: Losable for real: three wrong letters in one message lose (the game resets `lives`, the lives fragment's public state, on each `round_started`), and a 120 s jammer (`time_limit`, `on_timeout: lose`). Every gate seed set we tried had a losing bot, and the pro still wins.
A 450 ms decrypt beat between guesses keeps bot runs at 5–23 s, so they aren't over in a few taps, and `keyboard`'s required `key_state(letter)` returns exactly 0, 1 or 2.
Content stays parseable: every message is lowercase letters and spaces with `|` line breaks, at most 4 lines of 13 characters, so the letter grid always fits the console.
themes: star wars rebel spy code cipher decode secret message wordle word puzzle daily space

request: a pass-the-phone party game for a sleepover where we all build something together

design.pitch: Pass the phone and build one pillow fort together: Ana, Kofi and Mei take turns dropping a swinging pillow on top, and every pillow stays in its builder's colour.
design.verb: Watch your pillow swing side to side above the fort, tap to drop it on top, then pass the phone.
design.twist: One shared fort, three builders: each pillow keeps its builder's colour and initial where it landed, every wobbly drop squishes the fort narrower for the next friend, and a perfect drop fluffs it back out.
arc: Turns 1–3: Ana, Kofi and Mei each drop a first pillow onto the teal couch ('The fort starts with you.'), with a 'Pass to …' screen between turns.
Turns 4–9: the swing gets faster every turn, off-centre drops narrow the top (never below 44), and the pass screen shows a mini fort and the last drop ('Ana: Comfy! +9').
Turns 10–12: the fort climbs toward 'CEILING · SKY FORT +30'; land all 12 for 'SKY FORT!'. Wait 5 s and 'Arms got tired!' drops the pillow for you.
design.lose: A pillow whose middle misses the pillow below tumbles off ('Tumble!', no points); three tumbles and the fort caves in.
design.win: Get through all 12 turns (4 each) without three tumbles. A drop scores up to 10 by how centred it is, a drop within 6 px is 'Perfect! +15', and landing all 12 adds +30 for the Sky Fort; the top shows the team's 'Fort' total and the turns scoreboard keeps each friend's own.
juice: A perfect drop: 'Perfect! +15' in the builder's colour, a 'sparkle', 30 cream particles off the top and a success haptic, and the pillow lands 12 wider (up to 190).
Every landing: the pillow squashes from 1.12x to 0.94x, 14 particles in the builder's colour puff out and the 'Fort' total bumps.
Sky Fort: the twelfth pillow reaches the ceiling, the label turns to 'SKY FORT!' and 60 gold particles rain down with a 'levelup'.
design.look: A cozy living room at night: striped wallpaper, a moonlit window, a floor lamp, a purple blanket canopy strung with glowing bulbs and a teal couch at the bottom; warm and sleepy, indigo with gold light. Pillows are rounded cushions in each friend's colour (coral for Ana, teal for Kofi, yellow for Mei) with an inner seam and their initial; a pillow that misses tips up to 70° and falls off the screen, and lives are little heart pillows. Avenir Next.
design.voice: Warm, encouraging sleepover banter: 'The fort starts with you.', 'Tap to drop, Ana!', 'Arms got tired!'.

brief.intent: Three friends take turns dropping swinging pillows onto one shared fort; every pillow stays in its builder's colour
brief.competition: co-op build with friendly per-player totals

why_its_good: One shared fort and everyone's pillows: each pillow keeps its builder's colour and initial exactly where they dropped it, so the fort is a picture of who did what, and the pass screen shows a mini fort and the last drop ('Ana: Comfy! +9') before handing over.

Easy to learn, with tension in the room: a pillow stays up while its middle is over the one below, every wobble squishes the fort narrower for the next friend, and a perfect drop fluffs it back out, so the room cheers or groans on every drop.
A co-op goal on top of `turns`' per-player totals: land all 12 and the fort reaches the ceiling for a Sky Fort bonus; three tumbles and it caves in.
pitfalls_avoided: `playtest.progress` counts score, lives and turn progress, so bots tap through the 'Pass to …' screen instead of idling on it (with plain score, Bullseye Relay's pro bot took 61 s).

An 'arms got tired' auto-drop after 5 s keeps every turn moving, points land at release so lookahead sees them, and the fall takes only 600 ms, so bot runs end in 4–17 s (13–17 s for a full fort) and about a minute for people.
Respects HUD capacity: `turns` already fills `hud_bottom`, so the team total is one extra `hud_top` text (3 of 3), not a fourth node or a `shared_progress` bar that wouldn't fit.
